title: Practice Exam 5
description: An additional full-length 36-question simulated California Class C knowledge exam. Challenging level.

questions.question: A bicyclist ahead extends their left arm straight down with the palm facing back. The cyclist intends to:
choices: Stop or slow down
Turn left
Turn right
Wave you past
questions.explanation: A left arm down means stopping/slowing. Left arm straight out means a left turn; left arm bent upward means a right turn. Give the cyclist room to act.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Bicycle Hand Signals

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with no gate or signal, and brush blocks your view of the tracks until you are within about 90 feet. The maximum legal speed is:
choices: 15 mph
25 mph
20 mph
10 mph
questions.explanation: Within 100 feet of a crossing where you cannot see the tracks for 400 feet in both directions, the limit is 15 mph—the same as a blind intersection or alley.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — 15 mph Speed Limits

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is stopped on the right shoulder with red lights flashing as you approach in the right lane on a multi-lane road. The law requires you to:
choices: Move to another lane if you safely can; otherwise slow to a safe speed
Maintain speed and stay in your lane
Stop in your lane until it leaves
Move over only if directed by an officer
questions.explanation: The Move Over law requires changing lanes away from a stopped emergency, tow, or Caltrans vehicle with flashing lights; if you can't move over, slow down.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Move Over, Slow Down Law

questions.question: You are following a large truck on the freeway. To see ahead and let the driver see you, you should:
choices: Increase your following distance beyond the usual 3 seconds
Tuck in close behind to draft and save fuel
Stay in the truck's blind spot to be safe
Match its exact speed two car lengths back
questions.explanation: Trucks block your view and have large blind spots ('no-zones'). Hang back farther than normal so you can see around it and the driver can see you in the mirrors.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Trucks

questions.question: A truck is making a right turn ahead and swings wide to the left first. You should:
choices: Stay back and never try to pass on its right during the turn
Squeeze past on the right while it is turned left
Pass on the left quickly
Honk so it completes the turn faster
questions.explanation: Large trucks swing wide to make right turns. Passing on the right puts you in a deadly squeeze zone; wait until the truck completes the turn.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Trucks Turning Right

questions.question: You finish parallel parking on a downhill street with a curb. Besides setting the parking brake, turn the front wheels:
choices: Toward the curb
Away from the curb
Straight ahead
Toward the center of the road
questions.explanation: Downhill with a curb, point the wheels toward the curb so a forward roll is caught by the curb. Uphill with a curb, point them away.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking on Hills

questions.question: Which of these is a legal parking spot?
choices: 16 feet from a fire hydrant on a street with no parking signs
12 feet from a fire hydrant
Partly blocking a marked crosswalk
Across a residential driveway
questions.explanation: You may not park within 15 feet of a hydrant, in a crosswalk, or blocking a driveway. A spot clear of these, with no prohibiting sign, is legal.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Where You May Not Park

questions.question: A white curb means you may:
choices: Stop only briefly to load or unload passengers or mail
Park for a limited time shown by sign
Park as long as you wish
Load or unload freight only
questions.explanation: White = brief passenger or mail loading. Green = limited time, yellow = freight loading, red = no stopping, blue = disabled.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Colored Curbs

questions.question: A white rectangular 'KEEP RIGHT' sign with a downward-left arrow at a median means:
choices: Pass to the right of the divider or obstruction ahead
Slower traffic should keep right
The right lane ends ahead
Right turn only
questions.explanation: A 'KEEP RIGHT' sign at a median or island tells you to pass on the right side of the obstruction. It is a regulatory instruction you must obey.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Regulatory Signs

questions.question: A yellow pennant-shaped sign (a horizontal triangle) posted on the LEFT side of the road means:
choices: No-passing zone
School crossing
Yield ahead
Divided highway begins
questions.explanation: The pennant shape marks the start of a no-passing zone and is posted on the left. A pentagon marks school zones; a downward triangle is yield.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sign Shapes

questions.question: A diamond-shaped yellow sign showing two curved arrows forming an S warns of:
choices: A winding road with several curves ahead
A single sharp curve
A slippery road
A divided highway
questions.explanation: An S-shaped (winding-road) warning sign means several curves are coming. Reduce speed before the first one.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Warning Signs

questions.question: At a four-way stop you and the car directly across from you stop at the same time. You go straight; they turn left across your path. Who proceeds first?
choices: You do; a left-turning driver yields to oncoming traffic going straight
The left-turning driver, since they signaled
Whoever is on the right
You both go at once
questions.explanation: When two opposing cars reach a four-way stop together, the one going straight (or turning right) has priority over the one turning left across its path.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Right-of-Way at Stops

questions.question: You are about to enter a roundabout when an emergency vehicle with siren approaches. You should:
choices: Not enter; pull over before the roundabout to let it pass
Stop in the middle of the roundabout
Speed up to clear the roundabout first
Enter and circle until it passes
questions.explanation: Don't stop inside a roundabout. If you haven't entered, wait and pull aside; if you're already in it, continue to your exit, then pull over.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Roundabouts / Emergency Vehicles

questions.question: You drive out of a parking lot across a sidewalk where a pedestrian is walking. You must:
choices: Stop and yield to the pedestrian before crossing the sidewalk
Proceed because you are already moving
Honk and continue slowly
Yield only if they are running
questions.explanation: Vehicles crossing a sidewalk to enter or exit a driveway or lot must yield to pedestrians on the sidewalk.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Entering Traffic

questions.question: Eating a sandwich while steering with your knee in traffic is especially dangerous because it is:
choices: A combined visual, manual, and cognitive distraction
Only a manual distraction
Safe as long as you watch the road
Legal, so it must be safe
questions.explanation: Eating takes a hand off the wheel, your eyes off the road, and your mind off driving—the most dangerous mix of distraction types, even though it isn't specifically ticketed.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Types of Distraction

questions.question: Your phone is mounted for hands-free navigation. While driving, the law lets you:
choices: Activate or end it with a single tap or swipe, or by voice
Type in a new address as you drive
Scroll through a long menu at a red light
Watch a video on it in traffic
questions.explanation: A mounted phone may be operated only with a single tap/swipe or voice command. Typing, scrolling, or watching video while driving is prohibited.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Cell Phone Laws

questions.question: Passengers are arguing loudly and distracting you. The safest response is to:
choices: Ask them to settle down, and pull over if you still can't focus
Turn around to address them while driving
Speed up to end the trip sooner
Close your eyes briefly to calm down
questions.explanation: Passengers are a common distraction. Ask them to quiet down, and if you still can't concentrate, pull over safely until things settle.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Avoiding Distractions

questions.question: A left-turn signal shows a flashing red arrow. You must:
choices: Stop, then turn left when safe if not prohibited, yielding to oncoming traffic
Continue your protected turn unchanged
Stop and never turn until a green arrow returns
Treat it exactly like a green ball
questions.explanation: A flashing red arrow means stop, then proceed with the turn like a stop sign—yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before completing it.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Signal Arrows

questions.question: You may make a left turn on a red light only when:
choices: Turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street, after stopping, where not prohibited
Turning from any street onto a one-way street
Turning left at any intersection after stopping
Never—left on red is always illegal
questions.explanation: A left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street, after a complete stop, unless a sign prohibits it.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Turns on Red

questions.question: You want to move from the right lane to the center lane, but a car is just behind you in the center lane. You should:
choices: Wait, adjust speed, and move only when there is a clear, visible gap
Move over and expect the car to slow
Speed up sharply and cut in
Drift over slowly so they notice you
questions.explanation: Never force a lane change. Match the gap's speed and merge only when the space is clearly open and you've checked your blind spot.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Changing Lanes

questions.question: A solid white line between lanes going the same direction means:
choices: Lane changes are discouraged or prohibited there
You may change lanes freely
Traffic flows in opposite directions
The road is one-way
questions.explanation: A solid white line marks lanes you should not cross, such as near intersections or exits. Broken white lines mean lane changes are allowed.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Lane Markings

questions.question: Turning left from a two-way street onto another two-way street, you should complete the turn into:
choices: The lane just to the right of the center line on the cross street
The far right lane
Any open lane
The center left-turn lane
questions.explanation: Approach from the lane nearest the center line and finish the turn into the lane just right of the center line—don't swing into a far lane.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Making Left Turns

questions.question: Children are gathered at a bus stop as you approach in a school zone. You should:
choices: Slow down, cover the brake, and be ready for a child to step out
Maintain the school-zone speed and hold your lane
Honk to warn them to stay back
Move to the far side of the lane and keep your speed
questions.explanation: Children near a bus stop may dart into the street unexpectedly. Reduce speed and be prepared to stop, beyond simply obeying the limit.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Driving Near Schools

questions.question: A school bus ahead activates flashing AMBER (yellow) lights. This means:
choices: It is preparing to stop; slow and prepare to stop, as red lights will follow
You must stop immediately
You may pass quickly before it stops
The bus is moving back into traffic
questions.explanation: Amber lights warn the bus is about to stop. Red flashing lights and the stop arm come next, requiring a full stop from both directions on an undivided road.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — School Buses

questions.question: A posted school-zone speed limit, when children are present, generally applies within:
choices: 500 to 1,000 feet of the school, as posted
Two miles of the school
The entire city
Only the driveway entrance
questions.explanation: School-zone limits typically apply within 500–1,000 feet of the school as posted, when children are present. Watch for the signs and slow accordingly.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — School Zones

questions.question: After a couple of drinks you feel relaxed and confident about driving. That feeling is:
choices: Itself an early sign of impairment—alcohol reduces judgment first
Proof you are fine to drive
Only a concern above 0.08%
Helpful, since relaxed drivers are safer
questions.explanation: Alcohol impairs judgment and inhibition before coordination, so feeling confident is an early impairment effect, not a sign you're safe to drive.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Effects of Alcohol

questions.question: A second DUI conviction within ten years, compared with a first, brings:
choices: Harsher penalties, including a longer suspension and likely jail
The same penalties as the first
Lighter penalties for a repeat case
Only a fine, no suspension
questions.explanation: DUI penalties escalate with each offense in the look-back period—longer suspensions, bigger fines, mandatory jail, and longer DUI programs.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — DUI Penalties

questions.question: You are 19 and a breath test reads 0.03%. Regarding your license:
choices: It can be suspended—the under-21 limit is 0.01%
You are legal, since it's under 0.08%
You are legal, since it's under 0.05%
Only a fine applies, no suspension
questions.explanation: Under 21, any BAC of 0.01% or higher violates the zero-tolerance law and leads to a license suspension, far below the 0.08% adult limit.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Zero Tolerance Law

questions.question: Your off-ramp curves and posts an advisory speed of 35 mph. You should:
choices: Slow to about 35 mph after you leave the through lane, on the ramp
Brake to 35 mph in the through lane before exiting
Take the ramp at freeway speed
Stop at the top of the ramp first
questions.explanation: Keep your speed up until on the deceleration ramp, then slow to the posted advisory speed for the curve—don't brake hard in the through lane.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Exiting the Freeway

questions.question: Freeway traffic ahead suddenly slows to a crawl. To reduce a chain-reaction crash you can:
choices: Tap your brakes early or flash hazards as you slow, warning drivers behind
Slam on the brakes without warning
Swerve onto the shoulder
Speed up to find a gap
questions.explanation: Braking early or flashing hazards alerts drivers behind to the slowdown, reducing the chance of a rear-end collision.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Freeway Driving

questions.question: A pedestrian stands at the corner but hasn't stepped into the crosswalk as you near a green light. You should:
choices: Watch them closely and be ready to yield if they begin to cross
Assume no duty unless they are already in the road
Accelerate to pass before they move
Stop and wave them across against their signal
questions.explanation: Anticipate that a waiting pedestrian may step off the curb. Be ready to yield, but don't wave them into a crossing against their signal.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Pedestrians

questions.question: A bike lane's solid white line becomes dashed approaching the corner. The dashed section means:
choices: Cars may merge into the bike lane there to set up a right turn, after yielding to cyclists
Cyclists must leave the lane there
Parking is allowed there
The bike lane has ended permanently
questions.explanation: The dashed segment near an intersection is where motorists may merge into the bike lane (within 200 feet) to prepare a right turn, after yielding to bicyclists.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Bicycle Lanes

questions.question: A rural road is posted 55. In fog with about 200 feet of visibility, a safe and legal speed is:
choices: Well below 55—slow enough to stop within the distance you can see
Exactly 55, the posted limit
45, the automatic fog limit
Any speed, since fog isn't covered by law
questions.explanation: The Basic Speed Law requires you to stop within your sight distance. With 200 feet of visibility, a safe speed is far below 55.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Basic Speed Law

questions.question: Braking from 30 mph on a wet road compared with a dry road takes:
choices: A longer distance, because wet pavement reduces tire grip
A shorter distance, because water cools the brakes
The same distance, since brakes are unaffected by water
A longer distance only if the brakes are worn
questions.explanation: Wet pavement cuts traction, lengthening braking distance. Slow down and leave more following room when roads are wet.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Stopping on Wet Roads

questions.question: A tailgater is behind you and the car ahead may stop suddenly. The best cushion strategy is to:
choices: Increase the gap ahead so you can brake gently and avoid being rear-ended
Reduce the gap ahead to discourage the tailgater
Brake sharply to make the tailgater back off
Speed up to outrun both
questions.explanation: A bigger gap ahead lets you brake gradually, giving the tailgater time to react. Brake-checking or speeding up only raises the risk.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Managing Space

questions.question: A flagger in an orange vest holds a 'SLOW' paddle as you reach a work crew. You must:
choices: Obey the flagger and proceed slowly through the work area
Follow the posted speed limit and ignore the flagger
Stop completely until the crew leaves
Speed up to clear the zone quickly
questions.explanation: A flagger's directions in a work zone must be obeyed, like an officer's. Slow down, watch for workers, and expect fines to be doubled here.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Work Zones / Flaggers
